protocol.cross_statistics: Use 2025 development reference counts for ARI and equal-country survey mass for Jaccard. Match each wave point fit to the 2025 point fit by maximum weighted overlap. Keep this mapping and match each refit to its own wave point fit. Evaluate all run pairs within each perturbation. Minimum of lower deciles over all wave pairs, and all clusters for Jaccard.
protocol.decision: Among freshly confirmed candidates that clear all original requirements, select greatest k then highest minimum cross Jaccard and cross ARI. Report sensitivity passes separately. If none pass, report the best observed candidate and its limitations.
protocol.fitting: Independent native development fitting in each wave. Weighted K-means on globally aggregated identical answer vectors (exact squared-distance objective), 20 initializations, max_iter 300, tol 1e-4, Lloyd.
protocol.geometry: Six respondent-centred worry coordinates and mean at squared distance factor alpha*(1-beta)/6; both crime and severe weather very worried indicator at alpha*beta; fourteen harm indicators at (1-alpha)/14. beta=0 is the control.
protocol.question: Is there one shared encoding and resolution yielding independently fitted worry-harm clusters that correspond across 2021, 2023 and 2025?
protocol.reference: 90,395 complete 2025 respondents from 92 common development countries
protocol.resampling: 80% of respondents within each country or approximately 80% of countries within region and income strata. Same draws and seeds across settings. Fit every prespecified run.
protocol.shortlist: Up to three candidates. Include the largest k that clears all strict pilot criteria, then best minimum cross Jaccard under original native filters and cross ARI floor, then best candidate passing the analogous sensitivity filters or closest eligible candidate if necessary. For the three distinct places, ties by higher minimum cross Jaccard, cross ARI, k, and lower beta. If strict success exists and space remains, include highest-ranked candidate at another resolution that passes either set of complete criteria.

protocol.fit: 20 starts, tol=0, max_iter=300, aggregate equal-country survey mass of identical response patterns
geometries: one-hot categorical with equal question weight
protocol.ordinal_q: 0.05 to 0.95 by 0.05, plus every exact q of a historically confirmed passing setting in these four waves
protocol.scope: 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2025; all five harmonized worries; fit native development separately; same representation and k
protocol.selection: Find highest resolution passing original criteria, and strongest separately labelled sensitivities. Shortlist up to 5 from the development pilots. Select recursively only after fresh confirmation; do not alter fits or retain only agreeing runs.

coarse.shortlist_rule: five ordered pools: highest-resolution strict; best nonbinary sensitivity; best binary sensitivity; best strict-native; best remaining. Rank by cross Jaccard, cross ARI, k, ID.

strict_hierarchy.base: Each point fit and each refit has a newly fitted three-centre weighted k-means, q=0.75 and relative squared mean multiplier 1.5. Align labels to the verified 2025 parent definitions.
strict_hierarchy.objective: Find a four-wave worry-only model with all native cluster shares at most 40%, all original within-wave and cross-wave agreement gates, and clear descriptions.
strict_hierarchy.previous: Three exact worry-only clusters, C2 with a 44.63% share in 2019. Keep the shared parent fit and fit two centres within C2 independently in each wave.
strict_hierarchy.primary: Use all five worries in both stages whenever a candidate passes the original gates and has one compact common description per cluster.
strict_hierarchy.sample: Independent sealed seed [20261118,4024], 8 pilot and 50 fresh confirmation subsets per test per wave
strict_hierarchy.shortlist: Rank passing pilots by all five questions, minimum cross-cluster recovery, then unmodified ordinal coding and stable parameter order; retain promising restricted severity splits as separate sensitivity fits.
strict_hierarchy.split: Fit two weighted k-means centres using only the response patterns assigned to C2 by that fit. Compare five-question ordinal and categorical representations, then targeted worry-severity variants using both crime and water or one of the two.
